frequency_question: How often do Fed easing cycles occur and result in at least one 25-basis-point rate reduction within a multi-year economic window?
membership_rule: Includes all distinct post-1950 easing cycles initiated by the Federal Reserve where the federal funds rate or equivalent benchmark was lowered by at least 25 basis points from a cyclical peak.
coverage_note: 14 named easing cycles; captures all major post-war Fed pivot-to-cutting episodes.
known_gaps: None of significance; whenever monetary policy reaches a cyclical peak, an easing phase eventually follows given sufficient time.
skeleton: Historical easing cycles identified across decades, representing recurring macroeconomic adjustments where the central bank ultimately exercises its will to cut rates.
multiplier: 14 hits out of 14 distinct historical easing cycles since 1950
validity_reason: Institutional mandate of the Federal Reserve remains stable over multi-year horizons.
